A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KoPE research work. All 24 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT versus ViT+KoPE experiments on image classification, segmentation, vision-language learning, and ARC-AGI, together with ablations and attention analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the authors' segmentation results in Tables 2–3 and encoder-decoder ARC-AGI results in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B retain the same Kuramoto phase updates, data-dependent coupling, attention rotations, phase initialization and mixing, and task-specific adaptations. The added acknowledgment of earlier value-vector rotations does not alter KoPE's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet datasets, ADE20K including its complex subset, COCO, DataComp and 40-task CLIP evaluation, and ARC-AGI-1/2 with re-arc pretraining. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The ViT comparisons, ARC comparator roster in Table 5, and appendix controls remain unchanged. Miyato et al. (2024) is newly discussed as related work but is not added to any reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, model configurations, data handling, metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B and D. Correcting 'layer layer' to 'last layer' in Appendix B.6 matches the layer already specified in Figure 7.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same attention and synchronization analyses, matched-FLOPs controls, rotation and phase-mixing ablations, coupling and step-size sensitivity tests, initialization comparisons, complex-subset evaluation, and visual examples. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains mean±standard deviation and maximum results over five test-time-training runs, with the same description in Appendix B.5. Neither version adds different run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative examples remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, ViT+KoPE-B retains 46.94 ADE20K mIoU in Table 2, while Enc-Dec ViT+KoPE retains 56.8±0.7 on ARC-1 and 9.8±0.6 on ARC-2 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Lemma 5.1, Appendix C assumptions and lemmas, proofs, and training/sample-complexity discussion are retained. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable synchronization, improved training/parameter/data efficiency, structured visual understanding, and accelerated attention concentration. The code pointer and related-work additions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The synchronization and binding interpretations remain unchanged, as do qualifications about the simplified theory, the Gini metric as a surrogate, and Diabetic Retinopathy evaluation variability. Appendix E retains the same applicability discussion and future directions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and a GitHub repository address to the abstract; v1 provides no corresponding project-code pointer. Implementation and experimental details otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish added access information, not the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Miyato et al. (2024), GTA: A Geometry-Aware Attention Mechanism for Multi-View Transformers. Sections 3.1 and 6 acknowledge earlier value-vector rotations and distinguish geometric rotations from evolving Kuramoto phases, providing a limited refinement of attribution and positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and spelling corrections, including 'layer layer' to 'last layer' and 'SERT-PUP' to 'SETR-PUP', adds brief related-work explanations, and replaces the preprint notice with conference publication text. Section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The added text changes front-page formatting and main-text placement, including moving Figure 7 higher on page 7. All 12 figures and 14 tables retain their displays and contents apart from a spelling correction in Table 14; there is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer improves reproducibility documentation, while the GTA acknowledgment in Sections 3.1 and 6 improves attribution and clarifies KoPE's distinction from prior geometric rotations. Small editorial corrections also improve readability. These are limited gains: the method, theoretical support, and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and repository usability cannot be established from the PDFs.
